title: Dissolving and solutions
keyIdea: Some solids dissolve in water to make a solution; we get the solid back by evaporating the water.

kid: Stir sugar into warm water. The sugar seems to vanish. It has dissolved and made a solution.
Leave salty water in a warm place. The water dries up, and the salt is left behind.
adult: A soluble solid (salt, sugar) breaks into particles too small to see and spreads through the liquid: a solution. An insoluble solid (sand, chalk) does not, and can be caught by a filter.
Dissolving is reversible: evaporating the water leaves the solid behind. The mass is not lost; the dissolved solid is still there.

familyTip: Try sugar, sand and salt in three cups of warm water. Which dissolve? Leave the salt water on a sunny sill for a few days.
